sources.title: Writing for user interfaces — GOV.UK Service Manual
sources.version_or_commit: Live, unversioned guidance; published 2017-10-10, last updated 2018-04-16; no commit/version displayed.
sources.locator: Sections “Think about alternatives before you add more words” and “Keep copy short and direct”; displayed lines 81–96; page change history at lines 182–201.
sources.observed_operation: Read page and displayed change history; it recommends starting with less, adding help only when user research shows need, short sentences with one idea, important words early.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guidance concerns user interfaces and online scanning; its advice is not a claim that brevity alone improves comprehension or that long information should be removed when policy facts require it.
sources.applicability_to_case: Useful hypothesis for information order and mobile scanning. Transfer to print/bilingual course notices requires testing and preservation of all policy detail.

sources.title: Finding participants for user research — GOV.UK Service Manual
sources.version_or_commit: Live, unversioned guidance; published 2016-03-01, last updated 2026-09-22 (lead-time guidance revision).
sources.locator: Target groups and recruitment criteria; typical 4–8 participants for a round; accessibility, assistance needs, incentives and bias sections; page updates lines 241–264.
sources.observed_operation: Read live participant-recruitment guidance and update history.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Participants should be actual or likely users; research method determines sample size. A typical 4–8 is a planning guide for a round, not a statistical-power claim or guarantee of representation. Recruitment approach can exclude people; use varied routes and ask about support/preferences.
sources.applicability_to_case: Supports two small iterative formative rounds, sampling around actual course interest, language/reading comfort and access modes once known. UK government guidance is a method precedent, not local law or a proxy for the center’s audience.

sources.title: Getting informed consent for user research — GOV.UK Service Manual
sources.version_or_commit: Live, unversioned guidance; published 2016-05-24, last updated 2018-11-05 (withdrawal guidance revision).
sources.locator: Information-sheet format; evidence of consent; access needs; withdrawal sections, especially lines 108–158 and update history 172–191.
sources.observed_operation: Read consent, accessible-format, voluntary participation, withdrawal and data-handling guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Consent must be understood, voluntary and recorded; accommodate formats and support. The guide directs organizations to their own data-protection/legal advice, so it does not establish this fictional center’s legal obligations.
sources.applicability_to_case: Propose plain, translated/otherwise accessible information and consent only after language pair is known; use mock materials and minimal research data, with a real withdrawal plan.

sources.title: Using moderated usability testing — GOV.UK Service Manual
sources.version_or_commit: Live, unversioned guidance; published 2017-02-21, last updated 2017-10-03 (assistive-technology and ending-session guidance).
sources.locator: Purpose, 30–60 minute sessions, task design and neutral moderation at lines 78–145; page history at 195–210.
sources.observed_operation: Read guidance on checking understanding/task completion, comparing language/layout problems, non-leading tasks, likely users, interpreters/assistants and non-judgmental moderation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A moderated test identifies usability issues and ideas; a small formative study does not estimate population prevalence. Use personal data only when service and security conditions permit; a prototype may not support that.
sources.applicability_to_case: Supports scenario tasks and separate comprehension/task outcomes with non-operational prototypes; use fictitious enrollment details and no personal data.

sources.title: Planning and writing text messages and emails — GOV.UK Service Manual
sources.version_or_commit: Live, unversioned guidance; published 2017-06-21, last updated 2017-10-03 (transactional/subscription/personalised examples).
sources.locator: Transactional-message examples and channel selection at lines 72–129; concise content, first sentence, sender, next action/timing at 141–163; page history 192–207.
sources.observed_operation: Read conditions for email/SMS, examples confirming an already-booked transport trip, message length/preferences, sensitive-information safeguards, and next-step/deadline guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Transactional messages follow a user action; any automatic confirmation must describe the actual service state. The guide says to consider user preferences, length and whether contact details are permitted/current; subscription messages require opt-in. UK government security rules and infrastructure do not transfer automatically.
sources.applicability_to_case: A mobile-message channel is an alternative to investigate only after process and user preference checks. It must not imply a seat is reserved unless policy says so; do not add a channel or contact users in this stage.

sources.title: Confirmation pages — GOV.UK Design System
sources.version_or_commit: Current live pattern; page exposes no release version/commit or page update date.
sources.locator: Use/how it works at lines 51–55 and 125–152; required next-step/timing and record elements; known gap about transactions inside wider journeys.
sources.observed_operation: Read current pattern and example; it separates transaction completion from next steps, suggests a reference if one exists, contact details and a saved record; page explicitly says research is needed for a confirmation embedded in a wider task.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Use at the end of a transaction; details must reflect the real process. The pattern does not decide whether form submission itself reserves a place; it acknowledges unresolved wider-journey research.
sources.applicability_to_case: A useful service-state model for testing the difference between form received and place confirmed, only after the center verifies which state exists. Digital government transaction pages differ from a printed enrollment notice.

sources.title: Confirmation pages backlog discussion, issue #40 — alphagov/govuk-design-system-backlog
sources.version_or_commit: Issue #40 opened 2018-01-12 and marked published; no release commit shown on the issue.
sources.locator: Issue description and metadata, displayed lines 128–186.
sources.observed_operation: Read the primary backlog item documenting the pattern’s discussion/publication status and opening date.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Issue history records governance/publication, not a controlled user study or evidence that this notice pattern works in a community-course setting.
sources.applicability_to_case: Supplies a bounded implementation-history anchor; combine with the pattern page’s explicit known gap rather than claiming transfer evidence.

sources.title: Appointments service pattern proof of concept — Ministry of Justice Design System
sources.version_or_commit: Current live proof-of-concept page; no commit/revision identifier displayed.
sources.locator: Overview at lines 112–116; end-to-end context including pending confirmation, assisted digital, payment and unhappy paths at 292–321.
sources.observed_operation: Read the service-pattern description and scenario inventory, which names tentative/pending confirmation, payment to book, assisted paths and failure cases.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The authors explicitly call the patterns proofs of concept built to test usefulness. They are not an established validated standard and do not specify this center’s policy.
sources.applicability_to_case: A useful alternative map for service/process discovery: test whether pending/confirmed states, fees, help and failure recovery require distinct communication.

sources.title: Demography question development for Census 2021 — Office for National Statistics
sources.version_or_commit: Census 2021 question-development report; page has no commit/version date in its footer. Described Welsh-language testing occurred in 2017–2018; questions were finalized through 2020 legislation.
sources.locator: Section “Welsh language question development,” lines 444–459, plus report description at 96–97.
sources.observed_operation: Read account of focus groups and cognitive interviews with varying dialects and proficiency, specialist translation provider, and language/policy assurance group; testing led to different recommended terms.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This was a national census in Welsh, with a defined language, public-sector resources and statutory finalization. It demonstrates method and context sensitivity, not findings transferable to an unspecified language pair or course notice.
sources.applicability_to_case: Strong precedent for testing language-specific terms with varied proficiency/dialect and policy review. Do not assume bilingual readers or either language group are homogeneous; do not invent which variation matters locally.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 — W3C
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation WCAG 2.2 (2023-10-05); versioned normative standard.
sources.locator: Normative success criteria 1.4.10 Reflow, 1.4.12 Text Spacing, 3.1.1/3.1.2 language identification and 3.1.5 Reading Level; official TR page.
sources.observed_operation: Read the normative standard and conditions for web text reflow, programmatically determinable page/passage language, and the AAA supplemental reading-level criterion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Conformance applies to web content; Reflow has exceptions for content needing two-dimensional layout, Text Spacing requires applicable markup support, and Reading Level is AAA with supplemental content. A readability metric is not a comprehension study and the standard alone does not establish legal applicability.
sources.applicability_to_case: If a future digital version is in scope, use relevant criteria as a proposed accessibility desk check alongside participant testing. Do not apply WCAG as proof that printed notice/SMS is understandable or legally compliant.

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System live assessment — GOV.UK Service Standard report
sources.version_or_commit: Published live-service assessment report; no source-code commit or exact report revision identifier exposed on the page.
sources.locator: Assessment sections on accessibility fixes, support channels, user research and transparency/documentation of pattern research; lines 329–342 and 357–359.
sources.observed_operation: Read report findings that accessibility audits identified issues later fixed; support channels surfaced user needs; the panel called for more end-to-end research and better publication of research behind patterns.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The report assesses a public-sector design-system service and its users, not community course readers; assessed improvements and gaps are institution-specific.
sources.applicability_to_case: Shows a useful implementation-history practice—record fixes and unresolved questions and keep studying end-to-end process. Local notice/process history must still be reconstructed from actual center records and staff.
